summary: Defines MIB objects, in SMIv2 format, for managing source routes on end stations of Token Ring networks where IEEE source routing is used. It is now historic.

eli5.summary: Gauges for the route directions a sender writes on messages in a ring network.

questions: what is the 802.5 source routing mib
what is a routing information field
how do you manage token ring source routes with snmp
subtitle: SNMP objects for reading and managing the Token Ring source routes an end station has learned.

tldr.problem: Token Ring end stations that use IEEE source routing keep a database of routes to other stations, but there was no standard way for network management to look at it.
tldr.mechanism: The memo defines one SNMPv2 MIB table, the 802.5 Station Source Routing Table, with a route control value, the list of bridge and ring IDs, and a row status for each destination MAC address.
tldr.outcome: It is an incremental update to RFC 1748, written as a separate document only because RFC 1748 was further along in standardization. The RFC is now Historic.

today: RFC 1749 is now Historic. It updates RFC 1748 and the metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes it.

sections.title: What the MIB Is For
sections.content:
RFC 1749 defines a portion of the Management Information Base (MIB) used by network management protocols. It covers the managed objects that IEEE 802.5 end stations use to manage source routes on a Token Ring network where IEEE source routing is in use.

The memo is an incremental update to RFC 1748, the IEEE 802.5 MIB. It is documented separately only because of the maturity of RFC 1748 within the Internet standardization process. Where RFC 1525 defines the source-routing objects for source-routing and SRT bridges, this memo defines them for source-routing end stations.
sections.eli5: Some stations on a ring need to know the way to other stations. This memo is a standard list of questions you can ask a station about those ways.

sections.title: Source Routing on Token Ring
sections.content:
Source routing extends 802.5 by giving each ring in the extended LAN a unique ring number, and each source routing bridge connection to a ring a bridge number. A Routing Information Field (RIF) must be included in frames that need to cross more than one ring.

The RIF is a 2-octet Routing Control (RC) field followed by 0 to 8 Routing Descriptor (RD) fields of 2 octets each. The RC field carries an explorer indicator, the length of the RIF, a direction bit that says how to read the RDs, and the maximum frame length. Each RD holds a ring number and a bridge number.
sections.eli5: Each hallway ring gets a number and each door between rings gets a number. A message carries a list of those numbers so it knows which doors to go through.

sections.title: The Station Source Route Table
sections.content:
The memo defines a single table, dot5SrRouteTable, that holds the source routes known by an end station. The module is dot5SrMIB and sits at { mib-2 42 }. Each row is indexed by ifIndex and the destination MAC address, dot5SrRouteDestination.

  • dot5SrRouteControl: the 2-octet Routing Control field for the route.
  • dot5SrRouteDescr: the embedded sequence of bridge and ring IDs, using the SourceRoute type, an octet string of 0 to 30 octets.
  • dot5SrRouteStatus: the row status.

An entry is created when a Single Path Explorer or an All Paths Explorer discovers a route to a neighbor not yet in the table, or when an All Paths Explorer finds a better route, such as a shorter one.
sections.eli5: The table is a notebook with one line per friend. Each line says which hallways and doors lead to that friend and whether the line is still good.

sections.title: Static Routes and Local Destinations
sections.content:
It is unclear how many existing systems let network management create or delete static 802.5 source routes. The memo still supports them through dot5SrRouteStatus, but the compliance statement only requires read access to it, so stations without static routes can still comply. Only the active value needs to be supported, and write access to dot5SrRouteControl and dot5SrRouteDescr is also not required.

Destinations on the same ring as the instrumented interface should also appear in the table. For them, dot5SrRouteDescr is the zero-length string and dot5SrRouteControl has the corresponding value.
sections.eli5: Friends in your own hallway need no directions, so their line has an empty route. And a station does not have to let anyone write in its notebook.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The memo's security section says only that security issues are not discussed. It sets no access-control or protection rules of its own, beyond the framework it builds on, the SNMPv2 Network Management Framework of RFC 1442, MIB-II, RFC 1445 and RFC 1448.
sections.eli5: The authors did not write anything about keeping the notebooks safe from snoopers in this memo.
